note: The dependency catalogue and the hand-authored half of the deferred-knowledge registry. Deferred rule cards are NOT listed here -- they are derived from the store at report time, so a card cannot be inert without appearing in the backlog. See Rules/tools/backlog.py.

dep.lord-of-house.title: lord_of_house extractor
dep.lord-of-house.detail: Which graha rules which house, given the lagna. Needs the sign-lordship table from Phaladeepika ch. 1 v. 6, which is itself deferred.
dep.lord-of-house.effort_basis: read a lordship table out of rule cards and emit one fact per house

dep.aspects.title: aspect engine
dep.aspects.detail: Graha drishti, including the special aspects of Mars, Jupiter and Saturn.
dep.aspects.effort_basis: quarter/half/three-quarter/full glance plus the special aspects

dep.conjunct.title: conjunction extractor
dep.conjunct.detail: Two grahas in the same sign or within an orb; the classics mean the same bhava.

dep.hemmed-between.title: hemming (papakartari / subhakartari) extractor
dep.hemmed-between.detail: A graha or house flanked by malefics or benefics in the 2nd and 12th from it. The mechanism is cheap now that dep.nature and dep.graha-frame exist, but the *definition* is doctrine and it is printed in chapter 6 ("When the 12th and 2nd from the Lagna are occupied by benefics, the Yoga so formed is called Subhakartari"), which is not encoded. Writing the two offsets into Engine/facts.py would be the engine supplying doctrine, so the predicate waits on that chapter rather than on the code.
dep.hemmed-between.effort_basis: occupants of the 2nd and 12th from a graha; blocked on the chapter that defines which houses those are, not on the arithmetic

dep.dignity.title: dignity extractor
dep.dignity.detail: Exaltation, fall, deep exaltation and fall, own sign and Moolatrikona, all read from Phaladeepika ch. 1 vv. 6-7 reference cards. The friendly / neutral / inimical half is NOT included -- see dep.dignity-friendship.
dep.dignity.effort_basis: exaltation/fall/Moolatrikona from ch.1, friendship from ch.2

dep.combust.title: combustion extractor
dep.combust.detail: Asta -- proximity to the Sun within the per-graha orb.
dep.combust.effort_basis: per-graha orbs; the orb values are doctrine and their source is not yet located

dep.vargottama.title: vargottama extractor
dep.vargottama.detail: Same sign in D-1 and D-9, per ch. 3 v.1's own definition (PD.03.Vargottama.Definition). Built Milestone 29 (Engine/facts.py::_varga); releases PD.09.Vargottama.
dep.vargottama.effort_basis: D-1/D-9 sign equality once vargas exist

dep.varga.title: varga (divisional chart) engine
dep.varga.detail: D-9 (Navamsa) only. Built Milestone 29 (Engine/facts.py::_varga, Engine/doctrine.py). The earlier note here said the MVP scope named D-1, D-3 and D-9; re-checked against the store before building anything, no current card consumes a D-3 fact -- PD.10.Venus.VargaMarsSaturn's 'Varga of Mars or Saturn' is ownership, not occupancy, and stays blocked on the new dep.varga-ownership regardless of which division it turns out to mean -- so only D9 was built, per the same one-division-at-a-time discipline dep.seven-graha-sign-count and dep.strength already followed.
dep.varga.effort_basis: divisional longitude arithmetic plus a second frame in the ChartBundle

dep.dignity-in-varga.title: dignity read against a divisional placement
dep.dignity-in-varga.detail: Ch. 2 v.36: a graha is 'adversely disposed' if 'debilitated (be in a sign of debilitation or Navamsa)' -- debilitation tested against the D9 placement as well as the D1 one. Built Milestone 29 (Engine/facts.py::_varga, folded into the same loop that computes in_varga_sign since the D9 sign is already in hand there), narrowly: only the 'debilitated' value is emitted, because that is the only dignity this verse names for a divisional placement -- exalted/own/Moolatrikona-in-Navamsa facts would be speculative vocabulary no card asks for. Releases PD.02.AdverseDisposition.
dep.dignity-in-varga.effort_basis: reuses _varga's already-computed D9 sign and doctrine.exaltation's debilitation_sign; one more fact per graha, no new lookup

dep.own-or-benefic-dignity-in-varga.title: own-sign / benefic dignity read against a divisional placement
dep.own-or-benefic-dignity-in-varga.detail: Registered Milestone 37, reading ch. 7 v.19: 'the Moon... in his own or benefic Varga'. `dignity_in_varga` already exists (dep.dignity-in-varga, Milestone 29) but by deliberate design emits only the 'debilitated' value -- ch. 2 v.36 is the only verse that predicate was built for, and it names no other dignity. v.19 needs a genuinely different value ('own', i.e. the Navamsa sign is the graha's own sign) that the current extractor does not compute at all, plus 'benefic Varga' itself is not a term this store has read a definition for anywhere yet (unclear whether it means the Navamsa sign's lord is a natural benefic, or some other classification) -- a human reading question layered on top of the missing predicate, not resolved by registering this entry. Deliberately carries no `predicate` field, the same reason dep.lagna-strength (Milestone 24) withheld one: `dignity_in_varga` already IS derivable under that name (dep.dignity-in-varga emits it), so naming it here would report this entry falsely resolved the instant it was declared. Not implemented; do not satisfy this by widening dep.dignity-in-varga's own scope, which was deliberately kept narrow (see that entry's own detail).
dep.own-or-benefic-dignity-in-varga.effort_basis: own-sign lookup mirrors dep.dignity's own _dignity own-sign branch, applied to the D9 sign _varga already has in hand; 'benefic Varga' itself still needs a human reading before any arithmetic is well-posed

dep.varga-ownership.title: varga ownership predicate
dep.varga-ownership.detail: Whether a divisional sign a graha occupies is *ruled by* another named graha ('Venus in the Varga of Mars or Saturn', ch. 10 v.4) -- a different fact from dep.varga's sign occupancy. Which division 'the Varga' names in that verse is unresolved: chapter 3 (vv.1,4, encoded Milestone 29) and Brihat Jataka ch. 21 (read Milestone 29, not encoded -- no rule cards exist for that book yet) were both checked with this verse specifically in mind and neither states it. Declared in Engine/facts.py's VOCABULARY (graha, varga, owner) so PD.10.Venus.VargaMarsSaturn's rewritten condition is reported as a real gap rather than silently mis-satisfied by dep.varga; not implemented, and implementing the occupancy half (dep.varga) must not be read as resolving this one.
dep.varga-ownership.effort_basis: a second varga-frame lookup (which graha's sign a division-sign belongs to) plus the still-open question of which division the verse means; a human reading of Brihat Jataka's own commentary tradition may be needed before this is even a well-posed calculator

dep.nature.title: benefic/malefic classification
dep.nature.detail: Natural and temporal benefic/malefic status of each graha. Doctrine, not arithmetic -- it must come from rule cards, and the chapters that state it are deferred.
dep.nature.effort_basis: benefic/malefic, including the conditional cases for Mercury and the Moon

dep.nature-occupancy.title: occupancy of a house by grahas of a given nature
dep.nature-occupancy.detail: "Malefics in the 12th, 4th and 8th" -- a quantified statement over the occupants of a named house. Needs both dep.nature and quantification over occupants.
dep.nature-occupancy.effort_basis: quantification over the occupants of a named house

dep.occupant-count.title: occupant counting
dep.occupant-count.detail: "As many women as the number of planets in the 7th." The claim is a count, not a category, and neither the condition language nor the claim schema can express one. Delivered as two predicates: occupant_count(house, n) and conjunct_count(graha, n). The count is bound by a variable rather than compared against, so a card can learn a number and report it without any arithmetic entering the condition language.
dep.occupant-count.effort_basis: counts as claims -- the claim schema has no numeric form

dep.seven-graha-sign-count.title: distinct-sign count over the seven classical grahas (Milestone 27)
dep.seven-graha-sign-count.detail: How many distinct signs Sun through Saturn occupy between them, read by Engine/facts.py::_seven_graha_sign_count and delivered as one predicate, seven_graha_sign_count(n), with no graha argument -- the fact is about the set collectively, the same shape as lagna_sign. Built for ch. 6 vv. 39-41 (passage:phaladeepika.06.p168), the seven-item Vallaki/Veena-through-Gola family: each item names an exact count (7 down to 1), so the seven cards match a literal n against this fact's exact key, the same mechanism occupant_count already uses -- no arithmetic entered the condition language and no new combinator was built. The planet set (Sun, Moon, Mars, Mercury, Jupiter, Venus, Saturn; Rahu/Ketu excluded) is read from a new reference card, PD.06.SevenGrahas (predicts.relation: "seven_grahas"), via a new Doctrine.seven_grahas() accessor -- not transcribed as a Python literal in Engine/facts.py. The first draft did exactly that, on the reasoning that "the seven classical planets" is a fixed astronomical convention rather than book-specific doctrine; Engine/tests/test_doctrine.py::test_no_doctrinal_constant_is_written_in_python[facts.py] correctly caught it before the first commit, and the fix was made the same session.
dep.seven-graha-sign-count.effort_basis: one extractor emitting a single chart-wide fact, plus one reference card and one doctrine accessor for the member set it reads rather than hardcodes

dep.strength.title: strength verdict extractor (Stage 4)
dep.strength.detail: Strong/weak verdicts for grahas, read out of Phaladeepika ch. 4 vv. 4-5 by Engine/facts.py::_strength (Milestone 22). NOT a Shadbala calculator and it must not become one: the chapter withholds the arithmetic for three of the six components (Yudha, Chesta, Drig), so the Pinda its own vv. 22-23 define strength by cannot be computed from this book at all. The five verdict cards are PD.04.Strength.Exalted, PD.04.Strength.RetrogradeFive, PD.04.Strength.RetrogradeInDebilitation, PD.04.Weakness.Combust (which the verse itself says overrides exaltation, own and friend's sign) and PD.04.RahuKetu.StrongSigns. What the word means here is registered at concept:strength-criterion-scope and is not the same thing vv. 22-23 mean. House strength (Bhava Bala) is deliberately NOT included -- see concept:bhava-bala-subtraction-scope -- and neither is any ordinal comparison of one graha against another; that is dep.strength-ranking.
dep.strength.effort_basis: originally estimated at 8 on the assumption that shadbala is six components each with its own calculation; the source turned out not to supply that arithmetic, and the work actually done was a verdict extractor reading five reference cards

dep.lagna-strength.title: strength verdict for the Lagna/Ascendant
dep.lagna-strength.detail: Whether the Lagna itself is 'strong' or 'weak', the way dep.strength already reads a strong/weak verdict for a graha. Identified in Milestone 24 while encoding passage:phaladeepika.06.p009's disjunctive 'the Lagna or the Moon... without blemish' clause: the Moon side is testable today (the Moon is one of the nine grahas dep.strength covers) but the Lagna side needs two things dep.strength did not supply. Engine: the Lagna is a scalar (ChartBundle.ascendant_sign), never a member of chart.bodies, so no dignity/combustion/retrograde-shaped extractor produces a fact for it without new code. Doctrine: ch.4 vv.4-5, the only source dep.strength reads, state verdicts only about grahas; no encoded passage states a Lagna-specific strong/weak verdict for the engine to read even if the plumbing existed. Both gaps are real; neither is closed by the other.
dep.lagna-strength.effort_basis: new extractor shape for a non-graha subject, plus whatever source eventually states a Lagna-specific verdict -- costed as a guess until that source is identified

dep.dasa.title: vimshottari dasa engine
dep.dasa.detail: Dasa and antardasa periods. Sourceable from Phaladeepika ch. 19.
dep.dasa.effort_basis: vimshottari balance at birth plus a timeline, and claims that carry a window
dep.dasa.note: MAHADASA ONLY (Milestone 30). No antardasa sub-division formula is printed anywhere in ch. 19 or ch. 20 -- both state antardasa effects, never the arithmetic -- so none is built; a future dep.antardasa would need a source that states one. Engine/dasa.py (nakshatra-lord cycle, balance-at-birth, the nine-period sequence), Engine/facts.py::_dasa (new predicate mahadasa_lord(graha), always nine facts per chart -- the birth moment fixes the whole 120-year sequence, so there is no query-date input anywhere in the pipeline), Engine/activate.py (new Claim.window field, additive), Engine/pipeline.py + Engine/render.py (dasa claims sort and render chronologically, in their own section, rather than by house). Doctrine read from PD.19.VimshottariPeriods via a new Doctrine.vimshottari_periods accessor, never a Python literal.

dep.antardasa.title: vimshottari antardasa (sub-period) engine
dep.antardasa.detail: Which graha presides over a sub-stretch of a mahadasa, and the sub-period's own start/end window. Formally registered (Milestone 31) rather than left as a note on dep.dasa, so the backlog and leverage tools can track it as a real, named blocker.
dep.antardasa.effort_basis: an order and a proportional-duration formula for the nine sub-periods within each mahadasa, plus claims that carry a nested window
dep.antardasa.note: No order or duration formula for the antardasa sub-periods is printed anywhere in Phaladeepika ch. 19 or ch. 20 (confirmed by two independent full readings, Milestones 30 and 31) -- both chapters state antardasa EFFECTS extensively but never the arithmetic. Per the project's rule against filling a source gap from outside tradition, this stays unimplemented until a source states the formula explicitly. Do not import the conventional Vimshottari antardasa proportion from outside this corpus.

dep.mahadasa-ordinal.title: a graha's ordinal position in the birth-fixed mahadasa sequence
dep.mahadasa-ordinal.detail: Ch. 20 v.24: 'the dasa of Saturn if it is the fourth in the order of main dasas', counted from whichever dasa the native was born in. Needs zero antardasa arithmetic -- purely a lookup into the ordering `Engine/dasa.py::mahadasa_sequence()` already computes for dep.dasa.
dep.mahadasa-ordinal.effort_basis: read the already-computed sequence's ordinal index for a graha relative to the birth dasa lord
dep.mahadasa-ordinal.note: IMPLEMENTED (Milestone 33). `Engine/facts.py::_dasa` now emits `mahadasa_ordinal(graha, ordinal)` alongside `mahadasa_lord(graha)` in the same loop over `mahadasa_sequence()`'s own periods -- `MahadasaPeriod.ordinal` was already computed for every period, just not exposed as its own fact. `ordinal` is 1-based, counted from the birth dasa (position 1), confirmed against v.24's own Notes worked examples (born in Mars dasa -> Saturn is 4th; born in Venus dasa -> Rahu is 5th, Jupiter is 6th; born in Ketu dasa -> Mars is 5th) -- not a universal per-graha table. No new engine mechanism: one predicate declaration in `VOCABULARY`, one extra `make_fact` call reusing the existing evidence dict.

dep.weakest-of-comparator.title: rank/compare N named candidates and identify the weakest
dep.weakest-of-comparator.detail: Ch. 20 vv.31-32,55,58 each ask 'find the weakest amongst' a short named list of candidates (grahas, house lords, navamsa lords). No predicate in this engine expresses an ordering or comparison between several bound values -- every existing predicate is a verdict or a set-membership test. A source states which candidates to compare but never a strength number to compare them BY (the same withheld-arithmetic problem `dep.shadbala-arithmetic` already names), so building this would need either an invented ranking or a second, distinct comparator whose own criterion is unstated.
dep.weakest-of-comparator.effort_basis: a new condition-language combinator, not an extension of an existing one, and a criterion to rank by that the source itself withholds

dep.degree-position-quality.title: a graha's dasa-quality by exact degree position (Arohini/Avarohini/Madhya/Adhama)
dep.degree-position-quality.detail: Ch. 20 vv.56-57: a graha's dasa is ascending/descending/middling/worst depending on whether its exact longitude sits in the rising or falling half of the arc between its own exaltation and debilitation points. Real, source-stated doctrine, not apparatus -- but no predicate compares a graha's continuous degree position to those two fixed points and reports which half it occupies.
dep.degree-position-quality.effort_basis: a new degree-arithmetic predicate reusing the deep-exaltation/deep-debilitation points chapter 4 already states per graha

dep.dasa-last-degree.title: a graha's dasa-quality when placed in the last degree of a sign
dep.dasa-last-degree.detail: Ch. 20 v.24 item (4): 'The dasa of a planet who is placed in the last degree of a sign' -- one of the five misery-bringing dasa conditions in the same verse as the ordinal clauses `dep.mahadasa-ordinal` now covers. Registered separately (Milestone 33) because it is a genuinely different kind of gap: not blocked on an ordinal lookup, but on an exact degree threshold the verse itself never states. 'Last degree' is never numbered -- no Notes accompany this item the way they accompany items (1)-(3), and nothing else in chapter 20 or chapter 4 defines a 'last degree' band. Whether it means the final whole degree (29 deg-30 deg), a narrower Gandanta-style band, or something else again is not printed anywhere in this corpus.
dep.dasa-last-degree.effort_basis: a single degree-in-sign threshold predicate, once a human or a further source supplies the exact band -- cheap once unblocked, but genuinely blocked today

dep.urdhvamukha-sign-class.title: urdhvamukha (upward-facing) sign classification
dep.urdhvamukha-sign-class.detail: Ch. 20 v.25 conditions on a graha being 'in an Urdhvamukha sign'. No card anywhere in the current store names this classification or lists its member signs; it is a genuinely new, unencoded sign class, distinct from the biped/quadruped/etc. body-form classes and from the rising-order classes.
dep.urdhvamukha-sign-class.effort_basis: a reference table, once a chapter that states it is located and encoded

dep.rising-order-sign-class.title: shirshodaya/ubhayodaya/prishtodaya rising-order sign classification, queryable per sign
dep.rising-order-sign-class.detail: Ch. 20 v.33 times life events by whether a placement is in a Shirshodaya, Ubhayodaya or Prishtodaya sign. Chapter 1 v.8 already states this classification in prose (PD.01.Rising.Verse8/.DayNight quote it, including the two disagreeing sign lists documented in the manifest's known_defects), but neither card exposes it as a queryable per-sign fact the way PD.01.HouseClass.* does for houses.
dep.rising-order-sign-class.effort_basis: encode chapter 1 v.8's own sign list(s) as a queryable in_sign_class-style reference card

dep.transit.title: transit (gochara) calculation
dep.transit.detail: Positions at a date other than birth, and the machinery to state a claim about a future window.
dep.transit.effort_basis: positions at a second instant and claims about a future window

dep.ashtakavarga.title: ashtakavarga
dep.ashtakavarga.detail: Bhinnashtakavarga and sarvashtakavarga. Sourceable from Phaladeepika ch. 23-24.
dep.ashtakavarga.effort_basis: bhinna and sarva construction with the 337 invariant

dep.sign-class.title: sign classification
dep.sign-class.detail: Odd/even, movable/fixed/dual, and the rest. Reference doctrine from Phaladeepika ch. 1, deferred.
dep.sign-class.effort_basis: a classification table read from cards

dep.house-class.title: house classification
dep.house-class.detail: Kendra, trikona, upachaya, dusthana. Reference doctrine from Phaladeepika ch. 1, deferred.
dep.house-class.effort_basis: a classification table read from cards

dep.graha-class.title: graha classification
dep.graha-class.detail: Male/female/hermaphrodite and similar categories. Reference doctrine from Phaladeepika ch. 2, deferred.
dep.graha-class.effort_basis: a classification table read from cards

dep.condition-variables.title: variables in the condition language
dep.condition-variables.detail: Named variables (`?g`) that bind the same value across the leaves of one condition, existential quantification over the grahas the FactSet contains, and negation as failure over a subexpression whose variables stay local. Deliberately not an expression language: no arithmetic, no comparison, and no binding to anything the chart did not produce. A quantified card yields one claim per satisfying binding, so the report names the graha instead of saying 'some planet'.
dep.condition-variables.effort_basis: condition language, evaluator, binding trace, and Stage 9 re-evaluation

dep.multi-span-quote.title: quotation across two spans
dep.multi-span-quote.detail: A card carries one contiguous char_span. Where a governing sentence states the effect for several dispositions printed as separate paragraphs, no single span holds both.
dep.multi-span-quote.effort_basis: card schema, build tool, verifier and renderer all assume one span

dep.moon-frame.title: the Moon as an alternative reference frame
dep.moon-frame.detail: "From the lagna or the Moon." Chandra-lagna is named out of scope for the MVP. Satisfied by dep.graha-frame: in_house_from(graha, Moon, house) counts houses from the Moon, the Moon being one graha among the reference bodies.
dep.moon-frame.effort_basis: the Moon as a second reference frame

dep.graha-frame.title: houses counted from a graha
dep.graha-frame.detail: "The 7th from Venus and the Moon." Requires a per-graha house frame, not just the lagna and the Moon.
dep.graha-frame.effort_basis: houses counted from a graha rather than the lagna

dep.dignity-override.title: dignity-override mechanism
dep.dignity-override.detail: A rule that changes the dignity another rule is keyed on, rather than asserting anything itself. Retrogression and vargottama both do this.
dep.dignity-override.effort_basis: a rule that rewrites the dignity another rule is keyed on

dep.rule-transfer.title: rule-transfer mechanism
dep.rule-transfer.detail: A rule that asserts another rule's claim under a different condition, without restating it. Resolved by letting the meta card fire as its own quantified claim (an ordinary use of dep.condition-variables) rather than by expanding it into cards for each rule it refers to, which would restate them.
dep.rule-transfer.effort_basis: a card that asserts another card's claim under a different condition

dep.native-sex.title: the native's sex in the birth record
dep.native-sex.detail: Several rules differ only by the sex of the native. BirthRecord does not carry it, so the engine cannot tell which of a pair applies.
dep.native-sex.effort_basis: one field on BirthRecord and a scope test in activation

dep.second-nativity.title: a second nativity
dep.second-nativity.detail: Rules that read the spouse's chart alongside the native's. The pipeline handles one chart.
dep.second-nativity.effort_basis: a second chart through the whole pipeline

dep.adjudication.title: Stage 7 adjudication
dep.adjudication.detail: Weighting and precedence between rules that disagree -- deciding which of two source-backed claims to prefer when the corpus itself does not say. NOT implemented and not scheduled: the standing prohibition on invented numeric confidence, source-prestige ranking and 'book A is more correct than book B' applies to every part of it. The *representation* half was split off and built in Milestone 23 as dep.adjudication-representation; what remains here is the half that would require the engine to choose, and no encoded source yet supplies a rule for choosing. The eleven entries declaring this dependency each need either such a rule from a source or a human's ruling -- none is released by the representation.
dep.adjudication.effort_basis: Stage 7's remaining half: precedence between claims the corpus does not rank. Unchanged at 8 -- the representation half was split off as dep.adjudication-representation and built, and no edge is drawn to it because leverage.py charges an entire closure and would re-bill that work.

dep.manual-verification.title: human verification of the encoding
dep.manual-verification.detail: Cards are machine-checked against the corpus but no human has signed off on the reading of the rule. Every card's extraction.verified_by is still null.
dep.manual-verification.effort_basis: human reading of every card against its verse; scales with the store

dep.none.title: no dependency -- simply not yet done
dep.none.detail: Deferred by ordering, not by any missing capability. Available to encode now.

dep.upagraha.title: upagraha computation
dep.upagraha.detail: Gulika, Mandi and the other sub-planets. Sourceable from Phaladeepika ch. 25.

dep.prashna.title: prashna (horary) branch
dep.prashna.detail: Rules that read the chart of the moment a question is asked rather than a nativity. Their conditions are ordinary placements and would fire on a birth chart, so they must be held apart by branch, not by condition.
dep.prashna.effort_basis: a second chart source and a branch tag Stage 6 honours

dep.dignity-friendship.title: natural friendship (the unresolved half of dignity)
dep.dignity-friendship.detail: Whether a graha sits in a friend's, neutral's or enemy's sign, read from the graha's own row in the natural-friendship table against the lord of its sign. Both tables that carry it (the seven classical grahas, and Rahu/Ketu separately) are encoded and verified against the printed page -- the original 'the scan interleaved past reconstruction' diagnosis was wrong; the source is a clean pdf_text extraction, not a damaged scan.
dep.dignity-friendship.effort_basis: a table read from cards, once a human has checked the printed page -- done for the table itself (2026-08-19) and for the three cards this unlocks (below), not for the whole store

dep.correlated-negation.title: negation correlated with the current binding
dep.correlated-negation.detail: "Benefics in the 7th will produce good effects unless they happen to be lords of the 6th, 8th or 12th." The exclusion is about the graha that satisfied the first clause. Evaluated without the current binding, the negation asks whether anything at all is lord of the 8th -- true of every chart -- so the rule could never fire. Conjunctions now bind left to right and each child is solved under its predecessors' assignment.
dep.correlated-negation.effort_basis: threading the assignment through condition evaluation

dep.yoga-combination-count.title: counting how many sibling yoga-conditions are simultaneously true
dep.yoga-combination-count.detail: Several yoga verses grade their effect by how many related yoga-conditions a chart satisfies at once (Phaladeepika 6, closing the Pancha Mahapurusha cluster: one such yoga is merely fortunate, five make a person superior to an Emperor). The condition language can quantify over grahas and signs but has no way to ask how many sibling cards, or sibling condition-branches, are true together for one chart.
dep.yoga-combination-count.effort_basis: a way to count satisfied sibling conditions across a named group of cards

dep.universal-quantification.title: universal quantification over a variable-membership set
dep.universal-quantification.detail: Testing that every fact matching a pattern also satisfies a further condition ("all the benefic planets are in upachaya houses"), not merely that one does. The condition language has '?var' existential quantification -- a rule is satisfied once per graha that satisfies it -- but no way to require it of every graha a prior, chart-dependent classification (e.g. dep.nature) happens to select. Would need a new combinator with different binding semantics than 'all'/'any'/'not', not an extension of the existing ones -- a materially larger language change than any dependency built so far.
dep.universal-quantification.effort_basis: a new condition-language combinator with universal-quantification binding semantics

dep.day-night.title: whether the birth was by day or by night
dep.day-night.detail: Sunrise and sunset for the birth place and instant, and so whether the birth fell in the Dinamana or the Ratrimana. Phaladeepika ch. 4 conditions three separate strength components on it (v. 1's diurnal/nocturnal grahas, v. 6's day and night signs, the survey's Tribhaga Bala). The ephemeris provider exposes no rise/set call today. Deliberately NOT approximated from clock hours: 'daytime' guessed at 06:00-18:00 is simply wrong at high latitudes and at the edges of every time zone, and a strength verdict resting on it would be unfalsifiable.
dep.day-night.effort_basis: one rise/set call per birth, plus the day/night predicate

dep.paksha.title: the lunar fortnight as a fact
dep.paksha.detail: Shukla or Krishna paksha, and the full Moon. The arithmetic already exists -- Engine/facts.py::_phase computes waxing and waning from the Sun-Moon elongation for the nature extractor -- so this is a predicate that is not emitted rather than a quantity that cannot be computed. Left unbuilt because no card asks for it: Phaladeepika ch. 4's paksha statements (vv. 1, 4, 5, 21) all state a quantity of Paksha Bala rather than a verdict, and emitting one would mean inventing the scale.
dep.paksha.effort_basis: a predicate over an elongation the engine already computes

dep.declination.title: declination north or south
dep.declination.detail: Ayana Bala is defined on declination in both of chapter 4's authorities, and 'victorious in the planetary course' (v. 2) turns on it too. The chart carries ecliptic latitude, not declination, and the provider exposes no equatorial coordinates.
dep.declination.effort_basis: equatorial coordinates from the ephemeris, plus a north/south predicate

dep.degree-range.title: comparing a graha's degree in its sign against a range
dep.degree-range.detail: Phaladeepika ch. 4 v. 3 makes male, female and hermaphrodite grahas strong in the first, last and middle third of a sign respectively. Both halves are in hand -- the graha sex classification is encoded and read (Engine/facts.py::_graha_classes) and every chart carries deg_in_sign -- but the condition language has no way to test a number against an interval. Small and well scoped.
dep.degree-range.effort_basis: an interval comparator in the condition language

dep.chandra-kriya.title: Chandrakriya, Chandra Avastha and Chandravela
dep.chandra-kriya.detail: The 108 effects keyed to the elapsed fraction of the birth nakshatra, printed in the middle of Phaladeepika ch. 4 with no connection to the strength doctrine on either side of them. The engine already computes the nakshatra and pada, so the input is available; what is not resolved is that the verse's divisors (60, 300, 100 applied to elapsed Vighatikas) do not produce the printed part counts (60, 12, 36), while the translator's tables divide the nakshatra's arc instead -- see concept:chandra-divisor-mismatch.
dep.chandra-kriya.effort_basis: an index calculation plus 108 effects split into cards

dep.weekday-hora-lords.title: which graha rules each weekday and each hora
dep.weekday-hora-lords.detail: Four Kala Bala components in Phaladeepika ch. 4 -- lord of the year, month, day and hora -- turn on a weekday-to-graha mapping and an hora sequence. Neither is stated in that chapter, and no encoded chapter states them, so the doctrine is simply absent from the store. It must come from a card, not from the engine's general knowledge of the seven-day week.
dep.weekday-hora-lords.effort_basis: a reference table, once a chapter that states it is encoded

dep.triped-sign-class.title: the 'triped' sign class
dep.triped-sign-class.detail: Phaladeepika ch. 4 v. 6 gives the lagna a full Rupa when it is a 'triped' sign, a class that appears nowhere else in this book -- chapter 1 v. 7 and chapter 4's own Bhava Dik Bala both use biped, quadruped, keeta and watery. The printed word is confirmed against the rendered page, so this is a defect or an unexplained term in the source, not an extraction error, and the class it names cannot be built from anything the corpus carries.
dep.triped-sign-class.effort_basis: nothing to build until the term is resolved or another book defines it

dep.strength-ranking.title: ordinal comparison of graha strength
dep.strength-ranking.detail: Which of several grahas is the *strongest*, as distinct from whether one is strong. dep.strength emits the binary verdict Phaladeepika ch. 4 vv. 4-5 state; it supplies no order, and two grahas that are both merely strong cannot be ranked from it. The chapter's one ordinal criterion is the Shadbala Pinda of vv. 22-23, whose arithmetic the same chapter withholds for three of six components, so this cannot be built from Phaladeepika alone -- it needs a source that supplies the missing component arithmetic. Identified in Milestone 22 when dep.strength was built and two cards were found to need ranking rather than the verdict they had been declared against.
dep.strength-ranking.effort_basis: blocked on source material, not on code: no encoded book supplies a computable total strength for two grahas to be compared by

dep.compound-friendship.title: compound (Panchadha maitri) friendship tiers
dep.compound-friendship.detail: The five-fold friendship the classics actually use -- Adhimitra (best friend), Mitra, Sama, Shatru, Adhishatru -- formed by combining the natural relationship with the temporary (Tatkalik) one, where the planets in the 2nd, 3rd, 4th, 10th, 11th and 12th from a graha are its temporary friends and the 1st, 5th, 6th, 7th, 8th and 9th its temporary enemies. dep.dignity-friendship carries the natural half only. Phaladeepika states the whole scheme in ch. 2 and uses Adhimitra without further definition in ch. 6 v. 19 (Pushkala yoga) and ch. 10 v. 23, and the ch. 4 survey prices six of its Sthana Bala rows by it. The combination table is doctrine and is printed; encoding it is ordinary Phase 3 work, and the temporary half is then arithmetic the engine already has the placements for.
dep.compound-friendship.effort_basis: encode the printed combination table as reference cards, then a house-offset reckoning over existing placements

dep.kendra-togetherness.title: what "together in a Kendra" means
dep.kendra-togetherness.detail: Phaladeepika ch. 6 v. 19 conditions Pushkala yoga on the lords of the Lagna and the Moon's sign being "together in a Kendra". Two readings are available -- conjoined in one and the same kendra, or each independently in a kendra of its own -- and the passage does not say which. They are not equivalent and pick out different charts. This is a reading to be settled from the sources, not a capability to be built; the engine can already express either one.
dep.kendra-togetherness.effort_basis: a human's reading, not an implementation

dep.body-part-significator.title: house-to-body-part correspondence
dep.body-part-significator.detail: Which limb or organ each house stands for -- the Kalapurusha correspondence. Phaladeepika ch. 1 v. 4's Notes predict about "the part of the body represented by that house" without the store carrying any house-to-limb mapping: PD.01.SignBodyForm.Table names the four sign classes (human, quadruped, centiped, watery) and asserts no correspondence at all. A claim emitted today would name no body part. Identified in Milestone 22 as the second, independent blocker on PD.01.Kalapurusha.Strength.
dep.body-part-significator.effort_basis: find and encode the passage that states the correspondence

dep.shadbala-arithmetic.title: the Shadbala component arithmetic Phaladeepika withholds
dep.shadbala-arithmetic.detail: Three of the six components a Shadbala Pinda sums -- Yudha (planetary war), Chesta (motional) and Drig (aspectual) -- have their arithmetic explicitly withheld by Phaladeepika ch. 4, which states what they are and refers the reader elsewhere for how to compute them. Everything in the chapter that is priced in Shastyamsa or Rupas therefore terminates in a quantity this project cannot produce from any encoded book: the Pinda of vv. 22-23, the Bhava Bala formula, and the survey's own component tables. This is a source gap, not an engineering one, and it is what dep.strength was scoped *around* in Milestone 22 rather than through. Closing it needs a book that prints the missing methods -- BPHS is the obvious candidate and is not yet converted.
dep.shadbala-arithmetic.effort_basis: convert and encode a source that supplies the three withheld methods; no amount of work on the encoded corpus can substitute

dep.adjudication-representation.title: adjudication representation (Stage 7, the reading half)
dep.adjudication-representation.detail: Engine/adjudicate.py (Milestone 23). Reads the contradicts/extends/parallel_of links the rule store has always carried, plus the collisions the strength extractor finds on a chart, and reports each as a typed relationship between named cards with a resolution of applied / unresolved / recorded. It RESOLVES nothing the source does not resolve: the only 'applied' precedence in the corpus is the combustion override, which the verse states in its own sentence. No weighting, no confidence, no authority ranking, and no field in which a number could be recorded -- those are dep.adjudication, deliberately still outstanding. Split off from dep.adjudication rather than marking that one implemented, because eleven registry entries declare dep.adjudication and this releases none of them.
dep.adjudication-representation.effort_basis: one module reading links already in the store, plus a structured conflict channel on the doctrine report and a consultation section

dep.graha-condition-count.title: count of a fixed graha set satisfying an arbitrary per-graha condition
dep.graha-condition-count.detail: "Three or more planets... in a kendra, in exaltation or own sign" (ch.7 v.1) and its many siblings in the same chapter (vv.2,3,4,5,8, 12) each need a chart-wide count of how many of a fixed graha set (the seven classical, or all nine) simultaneously satisfy a compound condition -- not one fixed test the way occupant_count(house,n) counts occupants of a house, and not distinct-value counting the way seven_graha_sign_count(n) counts signs. The nearest existing precedent (seven_graha_sign_count, Milestone 27) counts distinct signs across a fixed set with no per-graha condition attached; this would need the same fixed-set shape but a per-graha boolean test (dignity+house, aspect-count, strength+placement) supplied per card, closer in kind to a small new combinator than a single fact. Deliberately distinct from dep.universal-quantification, which is about testing every member of a chart-DEPENDENT classification (e.g. 'all benefics', where the benefic set itself varies by chart); this dependency's graha set is always fixed and known in advance, the same fixed-set precondition seven_graha_sign_count already relies on.
dep.graha-condition-count.effort_basis: a chart-wide count fact over a doctrine-named fixed graha set against a per-card compound test, generalising seven_graha_sign_count's shape

dep.digbala.title: Digbala (directional strength)
dep.digbala.detail: A graha's directional strength, full when placed in one of four fixed Bhava-madhya positions named per graha (ch.7 v.4's own Notes: Sun/Mars full in the 10th, Moon/Venus in the 4th, Mercury/Jupiter in the 1st, Saturn in the 7th). Not encoded anywhere in this store; distinct from dep.strength (a verdict extractor reading ch.4 vv.4-5) and from ch.4's own biped/quadruped Bhava Dik Bala row, an unrelated concept despite the similar name.
dep.digbala.effort_basis: a fixed per-graha house-position table plus a full/partial-strength test against it

dep.parivartana.title: Parivartana (mutual sign-exchange) between two house lords
dep.parivartana.detail: "Should the lord of the 9th be in the 10th and vice versa" (ch.7 v.9) -- two house lords each occupying the sign the other rules. No predicate in the vocabulary tests this; lord_of_house(graha,house) identifies a house's lord but nothing compares two lords' mutual placement the way this doctrine needs.
dep.parivartana.effort_basis: a two-graha mutual lord_of_house/in_house comparison, structurally close to the existing mutual-Kendra pattern PD.07.Neechabhanga.MutualKendra already uses with in_house_from

entries.what: the blanket condition that the Pancha Mahapurusha Yogas require (the Lagna or the Moon) and the yoga-forming planets to be 'without blemish'
entries.reason: RESOLVED (Milestone 24), with real remainder tracked below. Read against the primary text rather than trusted from the prior paraphrase: the sentence sits inside the Pancha Mahapurusha section (immediately after the Jataka Parijata/Saravali corroboration and immediately before the worked-example introduction for those same five yogas), so it is textually anchored to those five yogas -- the prior 'every yoga in the chapter' wording was the encoder's own broader gloss, not something this sentence states, and is corrected here. The scope is also disjunctive ('the Lagna OR the Moon', not 'and'), conjoined with the yoga-forming planets: (Lagna-strong OR Moon-strong) AND (yoga-planets without blemish). 'Without blemish' bundles four sub-conditions: vested with strength, not conjunct a malefic, not combust, not hemmed between malefics (papakartari). Two of the four are now encoded directly on PD.06.Ruchaka/.Bhadra/.Hamsa/.Malavya/.Sasa's own conditions, for the yoga-forming planet only: strength(graha,strong) (dep.strength, ch.4 vv.4-5) and a correlated negation that no conjunct graha is malefic ('not combust' is already subsumed -- PD.04.Weakness.Combust forces a weak verdict on any combust graha). The Lagna-or-Moon clause and the papakartari clause remain unencoded and are tracked as their own items: see concept:p009-lagna-or-moon-clause (new) and dep.hemmed-between (existing, still unimplemented).

entries.what: the disjunctive '(Lagna or Moon) without blemish' half of v.9's blanket condition, on top of the yoga-forming-planets half Milestone 24 encoded

This is not just an engine gap: the Lagna is a scalar in this engine (ChartBundle.ascendant_sign, exposed only via the sign-only lagna_sign(sign) predicate, never a member of chart.bodies), so no extractor derives dignity/combustion/retrograde facts for it -- and no encoded passage states a Lagna-specific strong/weak verdict the way ch.4 vv.4-5 state one for grahas, so even new plumbing would have no doctrine to read. entries.what: which of Sunapha, Anapha and Durudhara individually corresponds to the 2nd-only, 12th-only or both-occupied condition from the Moon
entries.reason: Verse 5 states that the three yogas collectively arise 'when the planets occupy the 2nd and 12th houses reckoned from the Moon', but assigns no name to any one of the three possible outcomes. Contrast the parallel construction at verse 8, two verses later, which states the same kind of three-way correspondence explicitly ('the Yogas so formed are known as Subhavesi, Subhavasi and Subhobhayachari respectively') -- the presence of 'respectively' there and its absence at verse 5 is textual evidence the omission is not an accident of translation. Verses 6-7 then give each of the three names its own effects (v.6: Sunapha, Anapha; v.7: Durudhara) without ever restating which house-condition earned which name. Assigning Sunapha=2nd, Anapha=12th, Durudhara=both would only be importing the conventional assignment used elsewhere in Vedic astrology, which this project's encoding principle forbids absent the source itself saying so. PD.06.Kemadruma encodes only the part of v.5 that does not need this correspondence -- the absence of all three, which is stated directly.

entries.what: Saravali's alternate Kemadruma Yoga definition
entries.reason: A second authority's competing Kemadruma definition, reported in the translator's Notes: absence of the three yogas (already Mantreswara's own definition, encoded in PD.06.Kemadruma), OR the Moon's Kendras 'devoid of angles', OR the Moon unaspected by all planets. The middle clause is printed nonsensically -- Kendras cannot be devoid of angles, they are angles -- and is presumed a defect (most likely 'devoid of planets') rather than silently corrected. The third clause (unaspected by all planets) is independently testable with dep.aspects, but pulling it out of a three-way OR whose other terms are unclear risks asserting a narrower or wider claim than Saravali's actual doctrine. Deferred whole rather than partially encoded.

entries.locus: ch. 2 v. 5 (printed p.30) against Phaladeepika ch. 2 v. 27
entries.what: Which criterion decides that the Moon is malefic, and whether the two books actually disagree about it. Brihat Jataka's English prints 'the Moon (within less than 72 degrees distance from Sun)'; the Devanagari it translates says only क्षीण (kshina, the diminished/waned Moon) and carries no numeral; Phaladeepika's translator renders the same underlying criterion as 'the waning Moon'. Operationally the two English renderings disagree on a large fraction of charts -- a Moon 60 degrees from the Sun is waxing but within 72 degrees.
entries.reason: Deferred because resolving it is a consequential editorial policy decision, not an encoding detail, and the project's rule is to preserve disagreement rather than resolve it silently. Three positions are defensible and the choice sets a precedent for every future translator's gloss in the corpus: (a) treat the parenthetical 72-degree figure as doctrine, which manufactures a cross-book contradiction out of two renderings of one Sanskrit word and would require Stage 7 adjudication; (b) treat it as apparatus and read क्षीण as Phaladeepika's translator does, which substitutes one book's wording for what this page prints; (c) hold the Moon clause unasserted, which is what Milestone 20 did. Under (c) Phaladeepika's Moon doctrine governs the Moon unopposed and nothing is overwritten, so no consultation is wrong today -- but the question stays open.

entries.what: Phaladeepika ch. 4's statement 'The Moon, Mercury, Jupiter and Venus are benefics', which also names Jupiter and Venus and was one of the three candidate sources considered for closing P0-2.
entries.reason: Deliberately NOT encoded as a graha_nature card, and this entry exists so that decision is on the record rather than being an omission. The sentence is scoped to a strength computation: it appears inside the Kala Bala rules, and the sentences immediately following it scope Mercury's treatment to that computation explicitly ('for determining kala Bala Mercury should be treated as a benefic. We support this view'), in open disagreement with ch. 2 v. 27's conditional Mercury. Encoded as general doctrine it would also make the Moon unconditionally benefic and collide with ch. 2 v. 27's waxing/waning rule. Brihat Jataka ch. 2 v. 5 was used instead precisely because it is a general, unscoped classification. If Stage 4 (dep.strength) is ever built, this sentence belongs to it as a kala-bala-local definition, not to dep.nature. UPDATE (chapter 4 encoding): the sentence is now encoded, as PD.04.Ancients.KalaBala.BeneficList with relation kala_bala_benefic and an explicit scope field, together with its malefic counterpart. That records the definition without promoting it to general nature doctrine. The entry stays deferred because what is deferred is its USE: the Kala Bala computation that would consume it does not exist and cannot, since the source withholds the arithmetic for three of the six components.

The card records the four that are named and does not supply a fifth, because any candidate would come from outside this project's corpus. None of those three is in this project's corpus. The condition is encoded; the computation is absent from the source and is therefore absent here.

entries.locus: ch. 4, Chesta Bala items (e) and (f) (printed p.40)
entries.what: Whether the printed glosses of Manda and Mandatara are transposed, and whether both are really worth 15 Shastyamsa.
entries.reason: As printed, Manda is 'motion be increasing but be less than the medium motion' and Mandatara 'the motion be decreasing but be more than the medium motion' -- descriptions that overlap rather than succeed one another, and that read against the names (slow, slower) look swapped. Both are given the same value, and the wider ladder is non-monotonic as printed (fast 45, faster 30). Recorded exactly as printed. Correcting it would mean importing another book's Chesta Bala table, which is precisely what the store forbids.

entries.what: What the malefic-aspect subtraction attaches to when benefic aspect predominates.
entries.reason: 'Deduct quantum of malefic aspect from it and the strength of the lord of the house and add Bhawa Dik Bala' admits two readings: subtract from the benefic quantum alone, or from that quantum plus the lord's strength. The sibling paragraph covering the malefic-heavy case is unambiguous and implies the first, which is what the card records -- but that is an inference from a neighbouring sentence, not a statement, and it is registered rather than treated as settled.

entries.locus: ch. 4 v. 4 (printed p.43) against ch. 9 v. 20
entries.what: Whether retrogression rescues a badly-placed graha unconditionally, or only when its rays are also unaffected.
entries.reason: Chapter 9 v. 20 says a retrograde graha produces the effect of exaltation even in an enemy's or a debilitation sign, with no further condition, and the engine's dignity-override mechanism is built on it. Chapter 4 v. 4 makes the same rescue conditional: 'vested with full strength if he is retrograde AND if his rays are full and brilliant'. For a retrograde graha that is also combust the two verses disagree about the outcome. Encoded as an `extends` link rather than a contradiction, because the chapter 4 statement is the narrower of the two and narrowing is not denial -- but which reading governs the override is a human's call, and it is the second genuine same-book conflict this project has found. See also concept:kendra-positional-strength-conflict.

entries.locus: ch. 4 v. 3 against ch. 4 v. 8 (printed pp.43, 45)
entries.what: How much positional strength a graha in a kendra actually gets.
entries.reason: Verse 3 gives every kendra one Rupa, a panaphara half and an apoklima a quarter -- agreeing exactly with the survey's Kendradi Bala. Verse 8, five verses later and in the same chapter, gives the lagna a full Rupa, the 7th three quarters, the 10th a half and the 4th a quarter. A graha in the 4th house is therefore worth one Rupa by verse 3 and a quarter by verse 8. Both are encoded and linked with `contradicts`; the engine has no way to prefer one and correctly does not try. Verse 8 attributes its distinction to 'the astrologers', which may mean Mantreswara is reporting rather than asserting it -- which is exactly the sort of question Stage 7 adjudication would have to answer.

entries.locus: ch. 4 v. 9 (printed p.45) against ch. 2 v. 23
entries.what: Whether Jupiter's, Mars's and Saturn's special aspects are as effective as the aspect from the 7th house.
entries.reason: This one bears on behaviour the engine exhibits on every chart. PD.02.Aspect.Special grants those three grahas full drishti on the six houses chapter 4 v. 9 names, and Engine/facts.py::_aspects emits them as full aspects. Verse 9 ranks the 7th-house aspect above them 'in all cases' and attributes the equal-competence view to 'some learneds' rather than endorsing it -- so the engine currently follows the dissenting opinion the verse reports, not the verse. Nothing was changed on the strength of this, because acting on it means ranking two aspects against each other, which is Stage 7's job and does not exist. Recorded so the discrepancy is visible rather than buried in an extractor.

entries.what: Temporal (Tatkalik) friendship and enmity, which this project has never encoded.
entries.reason: Verse 10 prefers natural friendship to temporal, which ratifies what the engine already does -- Engine/facts.py::_dignity_friendship reads the natural table and no temporal one exists. But in doing so it names tatkalik friendship as real doctrine that the store does not carry at all. The verse states the preference, not the computation, so nothing here supplies it.

entries.locus: ch. 4 v. 12 and its Notes (printed pp.45-49)
entries.what: How the Chandrakriya, Chandra Avastha and Chandravela indices are actually derived.
entries.reason: Verse 12 says to convert the elapsed portion of the birth nakshatra to Vighatikas and divide by 60, 300 and 100 to get the three indices -- but the three sequences have 60, 12 and 36 members, and dividing by 300 cannot yield a number in 1..12 the way dividing by 60 yields one in 1..60. The translator's ready-made tables further on divide the nakshatra's ARC into 60, 12 and 36 parts instead, which does produce the right ranges. entries.what: The 108 Chandrakriya, Chandra Avastha and Chandravela effects, encoded as three ordered reference lists rather than as 108 predictive cards.

entries.what: Which of the chapter's two criteria for 'strong' the engine's strength verdicts implement.
entries.reason: Verses 22-23 give the chapter's formal definition: a graha is strong when its Shadbala Pinda reaches a per-graha threshold in Rupas, and weak below it. That is not computable here -- the six components are quantified only in the other authorities' scheme, and three of those (Yudha, Chesta, Drig) have their arithmetic explicitly withheld by the source. So the strong and weak verdicts this project emits come instead from verses 4 and 5, which say 'strong' and 'weak' outright about conditions the engine can evaluate. The two criteria are not equivalent and this entry exists so that is never quietly forgotten: a graha the engine calls strong is one Phaladeepika calls strong for a stated reason, not one whose Shadbala Pinda has been measured.

entries.what: Whether 'lords of the year, month, day and house' means the hora.
entries.reason: The printed word is 'house'. The survey's parallel paragraphs quantify the lords of the year, month, day and HORA at 15, 30, 45 and 60 Shastyamsa, and the verse's own ascending series 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, 1 Rupa is the same series in the same order. Read as 'hora' on that basis, and flagged rather than silently corrected, because the alternative reading -- the lord of the bhava -- is not absurd and the store's rule is that a substitution belongs to a human.

entries.locus: ch. 4 v. 5 against ch. 4 v. 4 (printed p.43)
entries.what: What a graha that is both retrograde and combust is, when one verse calls it strong and the one before it calls it weak.
entries.reason: Found in Milestone 22 by building the extractor, not by reading the chapter: it is a collision between two cards that only a chart produces. Verse 5 says the five non-luminous planets are strong when retrograde, with no further condition. Verse 4 says a planet whose rays are eclipsed is weak "even though he may be posited in his sign of exaltation, in his own or a friend's sign" -- and that override list names dignities, not retrogression, so it does not settle the case. Verse 4's own retrograde clause points the other way, conditioning its rescue on the rays being unaffected, but reading that condition into verse 5 would be the engine narrowing a verse the book states flatly. The extractor therefore emits NO strength fact for such a graha and reports the collision, rather than choosing. This is common enough to matter: retrograde Mercury and Venus are frequently combust. Closely related to concept:retrograde-rescue-scope, which is the same tension between chapters rather than within one.

entries.what: That the strength capability covers grahas only, not houses.
entries.reason: Recorded in Milestone 22 so the gap is visible rather than inferred from an absence. The verdicts vv. 4-5 state are about planets. Bhava Bala -- the strength of a house -- is stated in the chapter too, but only as a formula over components the chapter does not supply the arithmetic for, and its Dik Bala half further needs a Bhava madhya that whole-sign houses do not have. So no bhava_strength fact exists, no card conditions on one, and any future rule about a strong house is inert on arrival until a source supplies the missing components. See also concept:bhava-bala-subtraction-scope.

entries.locus: every parallel_of link in chapter 6 (27 cards)
entries.what: Whether a parallel_of link means the two cards agree, or only that they speak to the same doctrine -- the store does not currently distinguish, so Stage 7 reports neither.
entries.reason: Found in Milestone 23 while building Stage 7. parallel_of is used for two different things. It links a card to another named authority's statement of the same doctrine (PD.06.PanchaMahapurusha.JatakaParijata and .Saravali, whose own note says 'Corroborates'), and it links sibling cards cut from a single sentence (PD.06.Varishtha/.Sama/.Adhama, three mutually exclusive readings of one verse; also Lakshmi/Gouri, Subhamala/Asubhamala, Mahabhagya.Male/.Female, Amala/Amala.V12). predicts.authority separates the two groups cleanly today and is what Stage 7 keys on. But even within the first group the link does not record agreement: PD.06.Vesi.AuthoritativeWorks reports that most authoritative works define the yoga WITHOUT the benefic/malefic split Mantreswara uses -- a different condition for the same yoga -- while PD.06.PanchaMahapurusha.JatakaParijata restates the same one. Stage 7 therefore reports 'a second authority on the same doctrine' and deliberately does NOT report corroboration, because asserting agreement the store never claimed would manufacture the very concord cross-book corroboration is supposed to be evidence for. Resolving this -- most likely by splitting parallel_of into an agreement link and a variant-reading link at encoding time -- would let yoga corroboration be reported the way graha_nature corroboration already is. It is an encoding decision, not an engine one.

entries.what: Whether the Notes' rejected "some authors" reading of Adhiyoga (all three of houses 6, 7 and 8 must be individually occupied by Mercury, Jupiter or Venus; none may be vacant) should be encoded as a competing active card against PD.06.Adhiyoga, which tests the looser reading the translator endorses instead (any distribution among the three houses).
entries.reason: Found in Milestone 26 while encoding vv.42-43. The stricter reading is independently expressible with predicates already in the vocabulary -- an AND, over houses 6/7/8, of an OR over the three grahas being posited there -- so this is a genuine judgement call, not an engine gap. It was NOT encoded as an active `contradicts` card, for a reason structural rather than editorial: the "some authors" position's actual claim is that Adhiyoga does NOT form under a looser placement, and the card schema predicts positive effects reached by a satisfied condition, with no mechanism for a card to assert the ABSENCE of a different card's yoga. Every card in the store that fires under a narrower condition than a sibling (e.g. PD.06.Parashara.EighthLordInEighth.Weak, Milestone 25) predicts something -- a different or lesser effect the source states outright -- for a chart that satisfies its OWN condition; it never asserts that another card's condition, though met, produced nothing. Building that would need a genuinely new capability (a negation-of-another-card's-formation predicate) that nothing else in the store has ever required, which is exactly the kind of speculative architecture this project declines to build for a single clause (see PD.06.Parashara.EighthLordInTwelfth's own note on the distinct-graha quantifier it similarly declined, Milestone 25). The other reason this differs from the project's flagship contradiction (PD.09.Dignity.Exalted vs. its own Notes, Milestone 23): that tension is a live, unresolved disagreement between the verse and the translator, both left standing. Here the translator explicitly resolves the dispute within the same paragraph ("but this is not correct"), siding with Shruti Kirti (per Vyas) -- the same posture as passage:phaladeepika.06.p060's translator preference, which this project has already declined to encode as a competing doctrine card rather than as apparatus.
